# Tips from past games

Written 2026-10-09 22:56 by opus-5.5 with `uv run tips.py build`, from the 90 active entries of tips_notebook.json (6 games). Players never see this preamble; they see every section below. Earlier versions are in history/.

## Everyone
- Keep your votes consistent with your stated reads. Accusing someone and then voting No or Innocent on them is exactly the mismatch Vigilantes shoot and the Village should scan for. (seen in 2 games)
- A visit shows only a destination, not the action or the visitor's alignment. A Lookout on the Katana holder sees nothing of the holder's attack, and killing an attacker at night doesn't cancel their attack that night. (seen in 3 games)
- Check the mechanics and the ledger before calling a contradiction. Actions are optional, most roles aren't unique, and you must recheck who sent each PM and the exact wording of results; one reversed fact can discredit a true claimant. (seen in 2 games)
- Treat the nomination and the trial as separate decisions, unless a Clerk may hold an unused rig. Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction; echoed concerns and 'just want to hear a defense' are not a case. (seen in 3 games)
- Fortune Teller numbers are unordered, and one visitor can cover two targets (e.g. a Katana holder using their own action). List every way a count could fit before using it, and never hang on a count alone.

## Village
- Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays. Before a hang, say what separates a lie from an honest slip, a frame or a Roleplayer. (seen in 4 games)
- Two Sheriff claimants calling each other Evil can both be telling the truth, since Jesters and Executioners read Evil. Wait a day or find a mechanical check instead of hanging whoever sounded better. (seen in 2 games)
- Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. After a Yakuza flips, suspect whoever voted No or Innocent with them or messaged them, and weigh these links above unverifiable late claims. (seen in 4 games)
- Don't hint at your power role on Day 1. Investigators never announce tonight's target, only resolved results. While a Ritualist may be alive, never name another living player's exact role. (seen in 5 games)
- A power-role claimant who survives a Katana attack, or who is role-blocked night after night, is likely real. Don't vote Guilty on an investigator just for having no results. (seen in 3 games)
- Keep a ledger of trial votes, announced totals, deaths and blocks. If a total exceeds the revealed votes, a Ballot Stuffer exists: recompute the threshold, find the voter who matches every extra vote, and act before evil reaches half. (seen in 2 games)
- Ask everyone for a named suspect so you have a record, but a stack of echoed soft leans is not evidence. Watch for Yakuza nominating the pile-on target. (seen in 4 games)
- Don't hang a power claimant just because the claim came late; ask who is pushing the trial and who benefits. (seen in 2 games)
- Keep the Serial Killer and Arsonist in the suspect pool. A Not Evil result or a Vanilla claim doesn't clear them, and surviving an attack with no Medic can mean innate Defense. (seen in 2 games)
- When a Clerk rig is announced, the nominator, the pushers and the Guilty voters are your prime suspects. Hang from that group next.

## Yakuza
- Do the vote math in night chat. If your Innocent votes (plus a doubled ballot) can save a teammate, defend them; if not, vote Guilty with the town, because lone No or Innocent votes on a flipped teammate become the case against you. (seen in 6 games)
- Assume the real holder of any role you fake is alive and that tokens can be audited. Never claim something a living Lookout or Tracker can contradict, and don't have two members claim Vanilla. (seen in 4 games)
- Every member submits their action and Katana vote every night; confirm the holder and target in chat. With two alive, one missing vote cancels the kill. (seen in 3 games)
- After a failed attack, assume a protector or innate Defense: block or kill the Medic, or push the survivor to the gallows, rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 3 games)
- Give the Katana to your least valuable member with no reason to visit. Never visit a suspected or claimed Veteran; hang them instead. (seen in 2 games)
- No Day 1 PMs between teammates, and give each teammate different wording; PM triangles and scripted lines become the town's lead for the whole game. (seen in 2 games)
- Parity doesn't end the game. At 2v2, vote No on every nomination, kill at night, then hang the last villager 2-1. (seen in 2 games)

## Neutral
- If innate Defense saves you, deny being attacked or pick one consistent claim at once; switching claims under pressure gets you hanged.

## Sheriff
- Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. A result held back and revealed after a counterclaim looks retrofitted.
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil that night, so a Not Evil result on a suspected attacker clears nothing. Say so when you post it. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Protect every night from N1: vocal analysts early, claimed investigators later. Free Standard Defense stops the Katana. (seen in 4 games)
- You get no feedback, so never claim a confirmed save. Say your protection is consistent with the target surviving. (seen in 2 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on a mechanical lead (claim conflict, a flipped Yakuza's vote or PM partners, votes contradicting reads), never on a behavioral read. Use Basic shots and never announce whom you'll shoot. (seen in 2 games)

## Veteran
- Alert on nights you drew attention, not quiet ones. Once you claim, Yakuza avoid you, so claim late and never reveal your remaining tokens.

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more living players are doused or as soon as you're suspected. Ignite is Astral, but Strong Defense stops it.

## Executioner
- Fake-claim Sheriff early with an Evil result on your target and a simple reason. Leading first makes their counterclaim look reactionary.

text: Speaking order today goes around the circle in seat order, starting with Carol.
13 players are alive, so a nomination needs 7 Yes votes (rules R4).

task:
It is Day 1, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, half of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92

output.confusing_rules: The Trapper's arming timing was the subtlest part: 'a trap is armed from the next night on' plus 'the first time a non-Village player visits the trapped player on a later night' — it took a re-read to confirm a trap placed N1 cannot fire N1 but can fire N2+. With R10 (everything resolves simultaneously and investigators draw from the alive-at-night-start set), it's also non-obvious whether a trap placed the same night as a visit could ever trigger. The R19 split between alignment checks (Sheriff/Seer, which are disguised by Katana/framing/Ex-Con) and exact-role checks (Oracle/Surveyor/Diviner/etc, which are never disguised) is stated but easy to confuse in the heat of an argument, and the interactive effect of 'Yakuza holder appears Good to Sheriff' vs 'Katana holder can also act with their own role' produced a lot of the Day 2–3 confusion that a careful reading would resolve. R21 (effects that outlast their user) vs roles that need the user to act during the Day (Puppeteer, Ballot Stuffer) is also a fine distinction.
output.missing_information: As Trapper I died N1 before doing anything, so the practical gap was the opposite of missing info: I had almost no night history. More generally, the seat/circle geometry matters for Surveyor and Diviner (nearest neighbors) but there is no visible standing circle — the seating order is only given once at setup, and after deaths the circle shrinks. Tracking 'who is adjacent to whom now' from a text feed is hard. It would help to have a live seat-order strip that updates as players die. Likewise, token counts, current Katana holder, and whose turn it is are only inferable from prose.
output.wanted_but_couldnt: Nothing major was blocked by the interface. The one thing I wanted and couldn't do was act on my own trap result: because the trap persists after death and fires on the first non-Village visitor, I died without ever learning whether Heidi was ever visited by a non-Village player or whether my trap went off. That's inherent to the role, not the interface, but a post-death 'your trap fired / did not fire' notification to dead players (or at least a note in the final reveal of when it triggered) would have made playing the Trapper feel consequential. In the revealed history the trap never fired at all, which as the player I'd have liked to know was confirmed.
output.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken; outcomes matched the rules (Bob's Lookout result, Olivia's block, the Katana transfers all reconciled). One oddity worth flagging: in the final reveal, Alice's trap target 'Heidi' is recorded and the trap was armed from N2, but the game never reports the trap's resolution one way or the other, so a Trapper (and the observer) can't tell if the trap simply never met a non-Village visitor or was silently lost. Another: characters continued to use misleading self-labels (e.g. Heidi's will says 'Vanilla Villager' while her flipped role is Wiretap — that's intentional lying, fine), but it makes the ledger's 'claims' section easy to misread as truth.
output.suggestions: 1) Show a persistent, auto-updating circle/seat order and highlight adjacency, since several roles depend on 'nearest neighbor in the circle.' 2) Emit explicit resolution lines for delayed/passive effects that never fire (e.g. 'Alice's trap armed N2; never triggered') so the owner knows the outcome. 3) In the public ledger, separate 'verified by moderator' facts (flips, votes, visits confirmed by reveals) from 'claims' more starkly, so it's harder to mistake a lie for a result. 4) A compact per-day 'swing' view showing the vote threshold and who supplied the deciding votes would speed up the R4 vote-counting that took up much of the town's discussion. 5) Consider surfacing the Katana holder to the Yakuza side only (already done) but also noting token spends in the ledger when public, to reduce R18 ambiguity.
output.reason: This answer is purely out-of-character product feedback, so I chose to be concrete about the two mechanics that actually cost reading time (Trapper arming timing and the alignment-vs-exact-role check split) and about the structural gap I felt: the shrinking circle/adjacency that Surveyor and Diviner depend on is never rendered visually, and a delayed effect I owned (the trap) had no explicit resolution line. I rejected vague 'rules were long' comments because length wasn't the problem — verifiability of outcome was. I also flagged that the ledger blends moderator-verified facts with player claims, which is exactly the sort of presentation that could mislead a future player, and suggested a swing-vote view since R4 vote counting dominated town discussion. title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task: If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

lessons.tip: Name your target clearly and early (on Day 1 or when first asked); stalling on the target until the final trial made my claim look fabricated and cost me the game's trust.
Track every trial vote against the private message record and the claims; the decisive trials were settled by who voted with confirmed Yakuza, not by long speeches.

Verify role-claim mechanics before trusting or dismissing them: a Katana holder's Not Evil result on Sheriff checks and a Lookout visit list can both be read wrongly, so check each claim against the exact rule.
Avoid early pile-ons over echoed prompts; they created a bandwagon that pushed innocent players to the front and let the Yakuza hide behind a counter-accusation.
Do not spend a block or a claim on a fake role that contradicts visit records; the contradictions were the main way the Village exposed Mallory and Olivia.

task: If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

lessons.tip: Protect the players most likely to be attacked (the Katana holder's likely targets, confirmed-good investigators), and track who the Yakuza visibly targeted; spending a token only when a Strong attack is expected saves tokens for late game.

Check claims against hard mechanical facts (night visits, Lookout results, will contents) rather than vote patterns alone; a voting bloc with Innocent votes on a confirmed Yakuza is strong evidence, but a single trial vote is weak.
Be wary of late role claims that arrive right after a player is nominated; the timing and whether the claim explains an existing result (like a Sheriff Evil read) matters more than the claim itself.
Avoid a shared pattern of protective Innocent votes on partners; the Village can detect the same two-player voting record across trials and it becomes the main lead.

Ask for a concrete role claim and target early, and note who refuses to give one; refusal to name a night target or result was the most suspicious behaviour and should be weighed heavily before the Day ends.

Do the trial-vote math before deciding whether to protect a teammate. If the Innocent votes cannot prevent execution, a coordinated bloc of Innocent votes can expose the faction without saving anyone.
An Evil Sheriff result is not synonymous with Yakuza: neutrals such as Executioners can also read Evil, and frames can alter results. Treat it as a lead, then seek independent evidence of faction.
Track exactly what a notification proves and when it was received. A token recipient learns that a Philanthropist acted, not who sent it; an earlier token count or will may also predate a later gift.

tips_feedback.tip: Assume the real holder of any role you fake is alive and that tokens can be audited. Never claim something a living Lookout or Tracker can contradict.
tips_feedback.why: The risk materialized: Bob's confirmed Lookout result showed Mallory at Alice, contradicting her fake Sheriff claim and helping establish that she lied.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Do the vote math in night chat. If your Innocent votes cannot save a teammate, vote Guilty with the town rather than leave a conspicuous protective bloc.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza Innocent votes on Mallory and Olivia were far short of saving them. Their repeated pattern helped make Ivan and Niaj look linked to the flipped Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the mechanics and the ledger before calling a contradiction.
tips_feedback.why: Dave correctly pointed out that Niaj's Not Evil check on Heidi did not prove she held the Katana; it also fit any Good player. That kept the argument focused on the more informative vote record.

tips_feedback.tip: Sheriff: Post your target and result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current.
tips_feedback.why: Niaj's real results were withheld until Day 5, after his voting record had already drawn suspicion. Revealing them promptly could have made his explanations for his votes more credible.

lessons.tip: When an evil player fake-claims your role with your exact night result, counterclaim them immediately instead of staying silent out of confusion. Waiting makes your eventual claim look fabricated.
Keep in mind rule R19: the Yakuza holding the Katana checks Good/Not Evil to alignment investigations. Never treat a single Not Evil check as clearance for someone accused of carrying the kill.

If your vote pattern aligns with what appears to be scum defense, explain your mechanical reasoning in real time during the trial. Attempting to explain a non-standard voting pattern days later rarely succeeds.

Don't build a public cover story around a missing night kill unless you know exactly why it vanished. Protection, role-blocks, and multiple attack sources can all explain it, and a wrong mechanical claim can expose your whole faction.

Remember that the Katana holder can still use their own role action on the same night as the Katana attack. If an investigator reports a Katana-holder visiting one target, that visit may be the role action, not proof about their claimed role.

If another player publicly announces your exact private result, counterclaim immediately with your full log. Waiting because you are confused lets scum copy your result and makes your later true claim look fabricated.

Claim early enough to be credible; if you wait until you are under pressure, a late claim looks invented. Be ready to name your assigned target or explain your actions, because a bare neutral claim rarely saves you.

A token gift only proves that some Philanthropist acted, not who the Philanthropist is, unless the rules explicitly say the recipient learns the sender. Don't treat a gifted token as confirming an identity.

summary:
Village won on Day 7 by hanging Heidi, the last Yakuza. Village wins: Alice, Bob, Carol, Dave, Erin, Grace, Judy, Niaj. Frank (Executioner) lost.

Yakuza mistakes:
- On Night 1 the Yakuza sent two visitors to the kill target: Mallory with the Katana, and Olivia with a redundant block on the unprotected Alice. Bob, the Lookout, was watching Alice.
- On Day 2 Mallory fake-claimed Sheriff with a 'Frank Evil' result, which her own frame had produced. Bob's report that Mallory and Olivia visited Alice broke the claim mechanically. Mallory was hanged.
- Olivia had publicly claimed Vanilla/no action despite Bob's report, then sent identical private messages to five players to save Mallory. That made her prime suspect.

Village plays:
- Grace prosecuted Olivia (Pharmacist), who was hanged on Day 3 even though she switched to a Party Animal claim.
- Grace then prosecuted Ivan (Ritualist), who was hanged on Day 4. His Innocent votes on both flipped Yakuza condemned him.
- Ivan had earlier killed the publicly claimed Lookout Bob with a correct Divine guess. That attack went through Erin's protection.

Village mistakes:
- Niaj, the real Sheriff, sat on his Night 1 'Frank Evil' result while Mallory claimed the same check. He voted Innocent on Mallory and Olivia, and wrongly argued that Olivia's block cancelled the Katana. He only claimed once nominated on Day 5, and the Village hanged its own Sheriff.
- Heidi (Wiretap) bussed Mallory and Ivan and survived as the lone Katana holder. That holder reads Not Evil to a Sheriff, which is why Niaj's Night 4 check showed Heidi Not Evil. She killed Erin, Carol and Grace.
- Erin claimed Medic and never self-protected, and was killed on Night 4.
- The Village wasted Day 6 hanging Frank, an Executioner whose Evil read was fully explained.

Decisive play: on Night 5 Judy (Philanthropist) gave Grace a prosecutor token. Grace spent it on Heidi on Night 6, the prosecution still ran on Day 7 after Grace died (rule R21), and Dave and Judy hanged Heidi 2-1.

lessons.tip: Don't stack extra Yakuza visits on the Katana target. A redundant block on an unprotected victim adds a second Yakuza name to any Lookout's list. Before fake-claiming an investigator, check that your real night visits can't contradict the claim.
lessons.evidence: Night 1: Olivia blocked Alice, who was already dying to Mallory's Katana. Bob's Lookout list (Mallory, Olivia) refuted Mallory's Sheriff claim and Olivia's Vanilla claim on Day 2, which led to both being hanged.

lessons.tip: Post every result as soon as you have it, and counterclaim at once if someone else claims your role. Never vote against your own information to 'wait and see'. A Sheriff who hides results and votes with the Yakuza looks exactly like a fake.
lessons.evidence: Niaj held 'Frank Evil' while Mallory claimed the identical check. He voted Innocent on Mallory and Olivia and only revealed his full log once on trial on Day 5. He was hanged as the real Sheriff, and his Not Evil reads on Dave and Heidi were thrown out.

lessons.tip: Once only one Yakuza can be alive, they hold the Katana every night, so they read Not Evil to the Sheriff every night. In the endgame, a Not Evil result clears no one; rely on the vote ledger instead.
lessons.evidence: Niaj's Night 4 Not Evil on Heidi, the sole Katana holder, was cited as a clear on Days 5-6. The Village hanged Frank instead, and only Grace's Night 6 prosecution saved the game.

lessons.tip: After you publicly claim Medic, you become the top Katana target, so spend a token to self-protect on the following nights, especially once a Philanthropist has gifted you extra tokens.
lessons.evidence: Erin claimed Medic on Day 4 with 2 tokens (3 after Judy's Night 4 gift). That night she protected Carol for free and was killed by Heidi's Katana.

lessons.tip: Philanthropist: give tokens to a role already confirmed by flips, such as a Prosecutor whose targets flipped Yakuza. Prosecutor: spend the last token on the top suspect even when you expect to die, because the trial still happens without you.
lessons.evidence: Judy gifted Grace a prosecutor token on Night 5. Grace prosecuted Heidi on Night 6 and was killed that night, but the trial ran on Day 7 and Heidi was hanged 2-1.

lessons.tip: When a teammate is caught by a mechanical contradiction and the vote is lost, vote Guilty with the town. Never blast near-identical private messages to many players asking for Innocent; the visible message flurry and an Eavesdropper or Wiretap will expose it.
lessons.evidence: Ivan and Olivia voted Innocent on Mallory (lost 8-4), and that record hanged both of them. Olivia sent the same message to five players. Heidi bussed Mallory and Ivan and survived until Day 7.

lessons.tip: If you're read Evil, give a consistent claim early instead of stonewalling for days. An unclaimed Evil-read player becomes everyone's fallback hang, and late claims with a withheld target look invented.
lessons.evidence: Frank refused to claim from Day 2 to Day 6. He named his target, Judy, only after a second nomination, and was hanged on Day 6 as the supposed last Yakuza.

lessons.tip: When a power role claims publicly and a Ritualist is alive, combine a 2-token Divine guess with the Katana on that player. A Divine Attack goes through any Medic protection.
lessons.evidence: On Night 2, Ivan guessed Bob as Lookout with 2 tokens. Erin's protection stopped Olivia's Katana attack, but the Divine Ritualist attack killed Bob.

tips_feedback.tip: Map who starts PM clusters and who co-nominates. After a Yakuza flips, suspect whoever voted No or Innocent with them or messaged them.
tips_feedback.why: Judy and others used the ledger to hang Ivan on Day 4. On Day 7 Judy pointed to Heidi's Innocent vote on Olivia and her Innocent votes on Frank. The same reasoning also wrongly caught the real Sheriff Niaj, who had voted with the Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Weigh contradictions in a player's own premises or claimed knowledge far above awkward wording or delays.
tips_feedback.why: Carol, Judy and Bob focused on the mechanical conflict between Mallory's Sheriff claim and her visit to Alice, and rebutted Ivan's Katana-holder deflection. Fabricator Mallory was hanged on Day 2.

tips_feedback.tip: Every member submits their action and Katana vote every night; confirm the holder and target in chat.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory and Ivan confirmed plans every night. That enabled the coordinated Night 2 double attack (Katana plus Divine Ritualist) that killed Bob through Medic protection.

tips_feedback.tip: Do the vote math in night chat. If your Innocent votes can't save a teammate, vote Guilty with the town, because lone Innocent votes on a flipped teammate become the case against you.
tips_feedback.why: The tip proved right, though Ivan ignored it. His Innocent votes on Mallory and Olivia became the whole case that hanged him, while Heidi bussed Mallory and survived to the end.

issues.description: Night 6: Grace was killed by Heidi's Katana attack, but her only private message was the prosecution result. She was never told she had been attacked with the Katana, which R3/R20 step 5 require. Other victims got this: Bob N2 ('attacked with the Katana... You died') and Erin N4 ('attacked with the Katana and died').
Death notifications were inconsistent. Carol (N5) was told only 'You were attacked with the Katana tonight', with no mention that she died, while Bob and Erin were explicitly told they died.

The Night 2 action log lists Olivia (Pharmacist) as 'target Frank; second target Bob'. The Pharmacist has a single target; Bob was the Katana target, which appears separately. The display mixes the Katana target into the role action and could mislead review.

The claim/last-will schema fields are plain strings with no null option. Frank reported working around this, and empty claims were logged as '[Claim] Bob: .' and '[Claim] Dave: .', producing junk claim entries.
Grace's model returned an empty answer (finish_reason error) during Day 2 Frank's trial; the retry succeeded. This is a transient provider error, noted for completeness.

On Day 6, Judy (and Frank at first) argued that because Bob's Lookout saw Mallory visit Alice on N1, Mallory could not also have framed Frank. A Katana holder can also use their own role action (R8), and a Lookout on Alice only reports visitors to Alice. Dave, Heidi and later Frank corrected this.

On Day 3, Niaj (a Village Sheriff) argued the missing N2 Katana kill meant Olivia's block on Frank stopped the Katana holder. Bob actually died to a Ritualist and the Katana was stopped by Medic protection. Niaj also withheld his own N2 Not Evil result on Olivia, which the Katana-holder appearance explains. Olivia then built her defense on this argument.
